claims.text: 2G spectrum licenses were allocated on a first-come-first-served basis at 2001 prices in January 2008
The CAG report estimated a loss of Rs 1.76 trillion to the exchequer from the allocations
The Supreme Court cancelled 122 licenses allocated in 2008 on February 2, 2011
A. Raja resigned as Telecom Minister on April 2, 2011
A special CBI court acquitted A. Raja and all co-accused on December 21, 2017 due to lack of evidence

outcome.summary: The 2G spectrum scam led to the cancellation of 122 licenses by the Supreme Court in 2011. A. Raja resigned as Telecom Minister and was arrested. However, in December 2017, a special CBI court acquitted all accused due to lack of evidence. The scandal led to significant reforms in spectrum allocation policy in India.

title: 2G spectrum allocation scam
trigger: The 2G spectrum allocation scam involved the underpriced allocation of telecom spectrum licenses in 2008, causing a loss of approximately Rs 1.76 trillion to the Indian exchequer, leading to criminal convictions and the resignation of Telecom Minister A. Raja.
